name: instrument-buffer
title: Instrument input buffer: RF filter, 1.1 MΩ input, op-amp follower, 100 Ω output
about: A guitar or bass input that loads the pickup with 1.1 MΩ and drives the next stage with a low impedance. At the jack 2.2 MΩ to ground and an RF filter: 10 kΩ in series, then 100 pF C0G to ground (159 kHz). The input is AC-coupled (10 nF C0G) with 2.2 MΩ to the bias vref on the op-amp side; an OPA991 (2.7–40 V, rail-to-rail input and output, CMOS input) follows it, a 100 Ω resistor isolates the cable's capacitance, and 10 µF with 100 kΩ to ground makes the output DC-free. Maker-coverage BL-16.

ports.in: the instrument input: the jack's tip (a passive pickup wants about 1 MΩ)
ports.out: the buffered output, DC-free (0 V through 100 kΩ): the next stage, a relay contact, the output jack
ports.vcc: the op-amp's supply, 2.7–40 V: a pedal's filtered 9 V (block pedal-power, out) or a board's 5 V
ports.vref: the bias: half the supply – vref of block pedal-power, or a divider with a capacitor

components.label: {as}: input series 10 k (RF filter, input current)
components.notes: With the 100 pF an RF low-pass at the jack, 159 kHz; limits the current into the op-amp's input clamps.

components.label: {as}: input pull-down 2.2 M at the jack
{as}: output coupling 10 µF (plus at the op-amp)
components.notes: Polarized: plus at the op-amp side (vref), minus at out (0 V).

nets.name: in
nets.notes: The instrument's net: the pickup sees R2 ∥ (R1 + R3) = 1.1 MΩ in the audio band.

nets.name: rf
nets.notes: Behind the RF filter, at 0 V DC through R1 and R2.

nets.name: inp
nets.notes: The op-amp's input, at vref DC.

notes: R1 10 kΩ and C1 100 pF: an RF low-pass at the jack, 1/(2π · 10 kΩ · 100 pF) = 159 kHz – 8 × above 20 kHz (−0.07 dB there); 100 pF is small against the cable (66–164 pF/m, maker-coverage GTI 2). R1 also keeps the current into U1's input clamps within ±10 mA (OPA991 absolute maximum) up to about 100 V beyond the rails. Its thermal noise, 12.9 nV/√Hz, adds to the OPA991's 10.8 nV/√Hz – a smaller R1 for less noise moves the RF corner up.

Input impedance R2 ∥ (R1 + R3) = 1.1 MΩ – at least 1 MΩ for a passive pickup (maker-coverage GTI 1, GTP 14). R2 at the jack holds the jack and, through R1, the jack side of C2 at 0 V: no DC on the guitar's pots, no pop when the cable goes in. R3 biases U1 at vref; the OPA991's ±10 pA through 2.2 MΩ is 22 µV. A piezo wants 10 MΩ and more (GTI 10): larger R2 and R3, and load_min_ohm of the net raised.
C2 10 nF C0G: the high-pass with R3 at 1/(2π · 2.2 MΩ · 10 nF) = 7.2 Hz; C0G, not X7R, in the signal path (HINT.signal_ceramic).

U1 OPA991 as a follower (unity-gain stable, phase margin 60° at G = +1): 2.7–40 V, so the same block runs from 3.3 or 5 V and from 9 V up to an 18 V outlet. Rail-to-rail input and output: at 9 V and vref 4.5 V the output swings to within 55 mV of the rails (10 kΩ load; the data sheet's maximum, at 40 V). Its input pairs change over between (V+) − 2 V and (V+) − 1 V – keep vref at half the supply (2.5 V on 5 V) so the signal stays below.
R4 100 Ω: the OPA991 drives 1 nF directly, a longer cable with a series resistor (SBOS969F 7.3.4: 50 Ω in its figure); the loss into 100 kΩ is 0.01 dB.

C4 10 µF and R5 100 kΩ: the output is DC-free (0 V), as relay contacts and jacks want it (REQ.value/switch); corner 0.16 Hz into R5 alone, about 1.7 Hz into a 10 kΩ input. C4 is an electrolytic with its plus at U1 (vref).

Expected warnings: REQ.value/instrument counts R1 as a load on in and reports about 10 kΩ – the check takes every resistor on the instrument net as a load to a fixed level, R1 leads to R3 (2.2 MΩ to vref); LIM.v (grade polarized) sets out at the top of its range (+1.5 V) against the op-amp side of C4 at the bottom of its range (0 V, power off) – out is driven by U1 through C4 only, so the two never meet. Accept both in the sign-off with these reasons.

sim.json: an AC run from in to out shows the band – {"input": "<IN>", "output": "<OUT>", "expect": {"gain_db": [{"at_hz": 1000, "min": -0.5, "max": 0.5}], "low_hz": {"max": 20}, "high_hz": {"min": 100000, "max": 250000}}} (guitar domain on). A pickup's own resistance, inductance and cable capacitance (source r_ohm, l_h, c_f) come from its maker.
vref from block pedal-power; on a board without it two 10 kΩ from vcc to ground with ≥ 10 µF at the middle.

test.about: in and out become the nets T_IN and T_OUT; vref on the example's 3V3 – inside the OPA991's rail-to-rail input range on +5V (a real board: half the supply)
